question: Nearly 3 500 motorcyclists die on European roads each year1. This highlights the urgent need for additional measures to be taken to improve the safety of motorcyclists, including by raising vehicle safety standards.

In this context, Article 79 of Regulation (EU) No 168/2013 requires the Commission to consider extending the mandatory installation of anti-lock brake systems (ABS) on category L3e-A1 motorcycles that are placed on the market and to consider presenting a legislative proposal to that effect2. A study published in 2020 concluded that ABS should be a requirement for all new motorcycles placed on the European market3.

Bearing in mind that ABS systems have been proven to reduce road accident involvement by around 30 %, making a decisive contribution to saving human lives4, and that six years after the publication of the study in question, the Commission’s planned legislative proposal has not yet been presented, can the Commission answer the following: 1.
Why has it not yet submitted a legislative proposal for the mandatory installation of ABS on new L3e-A1 category motorcycles, despite the clear conclusions of the 2020 study?
Does it intend to propose a targeted amendment to Regulation (EU) No 168/2013 to that effect?
Alternatively, does it intend to extend the mandatory installation of ABS to all new motorcycles placed on the market in the context of a forthcoming revision of Regulation (EU) No 168/2013?
